score_evidence: 'SurePath mounted to a Humvee, 2025' paired with 'It can also be retrofitted to existing navigation systems' -> deployment_awareness_absence: real platform integration is claimed but ATO/RMF/CMMC/STIG/IL4-5 are never mentioned once across ~1,275 words

'Land and Air Defense: Convoy Navigation Object Detection Targeting Munitions UAVs Material Replenishment Threat Surveillance Close Air Support' -> operator_absence: applications listed as abstract capability tags with no operator voice, training story, or CONOPS anywhere in the pack

blind_spots.blind_spot: SurePath is pitched as retrofittable onto existing navigation systems and is already shown mounted on a Humvee, but the pack contains zero ATO/RMF/CMMC language for how that sensor's data gets authorized on the platform's network.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Retrofitting a sensor onto a fielded military platform means its data interface has to clear GFE integration and network authorization, not just a mechanical mount — a hardware company that's silent on this risks discovering the authorization requirement only when a program office asks for it, right as Series B math depends on contract revenue.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The public narrative and hiring are both centered on sensor performance (accuracy, jamming resistance, SWaP) rather than the acquisition/authorization mechanics of getting that sensor onto a program of record.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: It can also be retrofitted to existing navigation systems.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Munitions, Targeting, and Close Air Support are listed as defense applications with no mention of who trains an operator to trust or recalibrate a GPS-replacement sensor feeding those workflows.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A navigation sensor substituting for GPS in a targeting or munitions pipeline needs an established field trust-and-maintenance loop — sensor drift, recalibration cadence, and failure-mode training are existential once it's feeding a weapons chain, and none of that appears anywhere in the site's language.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team's NASA-space heritage (lunar landing, RPO precision sensing) frames the technology around measurement accuracy, not the field sustainment loop a weapons-adjacent ground/air defense application requires.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Land and Air Defense: Convoy Navigation Object Detection Targeting Munitions UAVs Material Replenishment Threat Surveillance Close Air Support

blind_spots.blind_spot: All visible hiring is core sensor R&D (mechanical, embedded firmware, silicon photonics, flight software) — no field integration, test, or compliance hires — even though the product is already mounted on a Humvee and pursuing a second Navy Phase II.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Moving from 'mounted on a Humvee for a demo' to fielded requires field/integration engineers fluent in vehicle GFE integration and platform certification; without that function staffed, Phase II SBIR dollars risk funding more sensor-accuracy iteration instead of the fielding push that actually converts a demo into an operational contract.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's leadership bios (NASA optoelectronics, USAF lidar, space business development) skew heavily toward sensor science and space/aviation business development, with no listed leader owning field deployment or DoD integration/compliance.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Senior Embedded Firmware/Flight Software Engineer ... Silicon Photonics Engineer ... Flight Systems Software Developer

opener_hook: SurePath was mounted to a Humvee in 2025 and Munitions and Targeting are listed as defense applications — nothing on the site addresses who calibrates or trains an operator to trust a GPS-replacement sensor feeding a targeting pipeline.
what_they_do: NASA-derived laser/lidar navigation sensor (SurePath) that provides GPS-independent position and velocity data for vehicles and platforms in jammed or GPS-denied environments, sold dual-use into both commercial and defense/space markets.
